newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt prices mixed, spreads narrow a tad.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt prices mixed, spreads narrow a tad.

text.p: Emerging market bonds ended mostly mixed after hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan permeated the market, traders said.
Greenspan told Congress Thursday that the U.S. economy retains a "great deal of vigor," and he again highlighted the Fed's responsibility to act preemptively against inflation expectations.
These comments sparked renewed debate about the Fed's intentions, changing the views of several economists on Wall Street.
If the Fed decides to rein in credit next week, as many economists now expect, several analysts said yield spreads of Brady debt might widen temporarily.
Basically, the emerging debt market has already priced in a a 25-basis-point interest-rate hike, said Jim Nash, Latin America economist at Nomura Securities.
"There might be some temporary backing up of the long bond and you might see that also reflected in spreads of various emerging market borrowings," Nash said.
In the broader Latin market, emerging market traders said yield spreads to Treasuries were tighter by about five to 10 basis points and trading volume was thin to steady.
"Things are pretty quiet," one U.S.-based trader said, adding that "we're just watching the Treasury market."
In the U.S. government market, the benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond is trading up 11/32 at 95-26/32 to yield 6.96 percent in late New York session.
In Latin Bradys, market sources said client interest leaned toward Brazil, Argentina and Mexico.
Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR firmed 1/2 to 76-1/2 bid.

"People think that 'C' bonds in particular have been hurt pretty badly in the (recent) selloff, therefore, we're seeing some client flow there ... and some institutional buying," said one head trader at a U.S. investment bank.
Argentina Brady bonds were also relatively active, with Argentina PARs AR4C23=RR up 1/2 at 64-3/8 bid and FRBs ARFLC05=RR up 3/8 at 90 bid.
Mexico PARs MX625L19=RR inched 1/4 higher to bid 72-5/8.
More broadly, Russian dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR fell 3/4 to bid 81-3/8.
A Reuters poll on Thursday found 34 of 48 economists see the Fed raising the key federal funds target rate 25-basis points at the central bank's policy meeting on Tuesday.
